target_columns.name: policy_id
target_columns.transformation: Inner merge key between premiums and policies (BY policy_id), passed through unchanged

target_columns.name: product_line
target_columns.transformation: Passed through from policies after merge; also used as the BY-group/partition key for the running total

target_columns.name: region
target_columns.transformation: Passed through from policies after merge, no transformation

target_columns.name: collection_delay_days
target_columns.transformation: collected_date minus period_start (date arithmetic, result in days)

target_columns.name: aging_bucket
target_columns.transformation: Nested IF-THEN/ELSE on collection_delay_days: <=0 'On Time', <=30 '1-30 Days', <=60 '31-60 Days', else '60+ Days'

target_columns.name: running_overdue_total
target_columns.transformation: Cumulative sum of premium_amount for rows where aging_bucket != 'On Time', accumulated in product_line + policy_id sort order, reset to 0 at the first row of each product_line BY-group (RETAIN pattern)

quirks: running_overdue_total is a sort-order-dependent cumulative sum (SAS RETAIN) reset at each product_line BY-group boundary; Spark has no guaranteed row order, so this must be reimplemented as a window function with partitionBy(product_line).orderBy(policy_id) matching the exact 'proc sort by product_line policy_id' order used in the legacy job, or results will diverge row-by-row

In SAS, a missing/null numeric value sorts as the lowest possible value, so if collected_date or period_start is missing, collection_delay_days becomes missing (.) and the first condition 'collection_delay_days <= 0' evaluates TRUE -- meaning uncollected/null premiums silently fall into the 'On Time' bucket rather than erroring or being excluded; this null-handling quirk must be preserved explicitly (e.g. via equivalent CASE WHEN ordering) since most SQL/Spark engines treat NULL comparisons as UNKNOWN/false, not low

The merge 'if in_prem and in_pol' is an inner-join; premiums with no matching policy_id (or vice versa) are silently dropped -- no explicit error or logging, must preserve as an inner join not left/outer

Two separate proc sort steps exist: first by policy_id (for the merge), then by product_line/policy_id (for the running-total BY-group logic) -- both orderings matter and must not be collapsed into one

FORMAT statement (8., $10., 12.2) only affects display/report rendering in SAS, not the underlying stored values -- reconciliation must compare raw numeric/string values, not formatted text, and any report-layer rounding to 2 decimals for running_overdue_total should be applied only at presentation time, not persisted as a precision change

aging_bucket boundaries are inclusive on the upper end (<=30, <=60) with no explicit lower bound other than 0, so negative delay (premium collected before period_start) is classified as 'On Time' -- preserve this edge case rather than 'fixing' it to e.g. a separate 'Early' bucket
